response.answer:
The Pragati Scholarship includes schemes designed for girl students pursuing technical education, specifically covering technical degrees and technical diplomas. 

For both the technical degree and technical diploma schemes, the annual scholarship amount is INR 50,000, provided as a lump sum. The funds can be used for purposes such as college fees, a computer, stationery, books, equipment, and software. Applications for both programs are submitted online through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), and payment status can be tracked via PFMS.

Key details for each program include:

Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Degree):
- Target group: Girl students
- Maximum duration: 4 years for first-year admission, or 3 years for second-year lateral entry.

Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Diploma):
- Target group: Girl students
- Maximum duration: 3 years for first-year admission, or 2 years for second-year lateral entry.

General exclusions and conditions apply to both schemes, such as:
- Students who fail or drop out in a subsequent year are not eligible for further scholarship.
- Receiving financial assistance, salary, stipend, or another scholarship from a different source during the course makes a student ineligible to continue.
- A gap of more than two years between passing the qualifying examination and admission is not allowed.
- No more than two girl children from the same family can receive the scholarship.

results.question: Who is eligible for the GATE/GPAT scholarship?

response.answer:
To be eligible for the Post Graduate Scholarship Scheme for GATE/GPAT Qualified Students-AICTE, students must meet the following criteria:

- Must have a valid GATE/CEED score at the time of admission.
- Must be admitted as a full-time scholar to an AICTE-approved M.E., M.Tech., or M.Des. program in an AICTE-approved institution or university department. The scholarship is subject to the approved intake of the program.
- Final-year students of eligible dual-degree integrated programs may receive the scholarship from the 9th semester for one year.

There are also specific exclusions to keep in mind:

- Foreign students are not eligible.
- Sponsored candidates are not eligible.
- Candidates admitted through management quota are not eligible.
- Students receiving financial assistance from another organization cannot receive the AICTE scholarship during the period of such assistance.
- Passed-out students taking second-time admission after re-qualifying GATE/CEED who already received an AICTE or other centrally funded institution scholarship are not eligible.

The scholarship authority makes the final eligibility decision, so please check with official channels for verification.

results.question: What documents are required for the Post Graduate Indira Gandhi Scholarship?

response.answer:
For the Post Graduate Indira Gandhi Scholarship For Single Girl Child, the required documents depend on who submits them:

Documents to be submitted by the student include:
- Aadhaar Card
- Proof of admission into a recognized Master's degree course in an institute located in India and recognized by the UGC
- Joining report as per Annexure-I
- Affidavit regarding Single Girl Child status as per Annexure-II
- Copy of the Bank Passbook
- Birth Certificate or Class 10th Marksheet

Documents to be submitted by the institution include:
- Progress Report after completion of the first year along with the percentage of marks obtained by the candidate
- Funds Utilization Certificate after completion of the first year

results.question: Tell me about scholarships for students with disabilities.

response.answer:
There are multiple scholarship schemes available for students with disabilities, depending on their level of education. 

Pre Matric Scholarship For Students With Disabilities
This scheme is targeted at pre-matric students with disabilities. Its objective is to support students with disabilities in continuing their education, developing skills for livelihood, and improving their ability to live with dignity despite physical, financial, psychological, and other barriers. The scheme covers specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Required documents typically include a photograph, proof of age, a certificate of disability issued by the competent authority, an income certificate, a tuition fee receipt, the last academic qualification certificate, and bank details of the applicant or parent/guardian. Note that there is an interesting detail regarding its application: the source states the scheme is implemented offline by DEPwD, while the application process section specifies online application through NSP.

Post Matric Scholarship Students With Disabilities
This scheme is intended for post-matric students, supporting them in pursuing further education, preparing for livelihood, and finding a dignified place in society. It covers students with specified disabilities defined in the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Required documents include a photograph, proof of age, a certificate of disability under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, an income certificate, a tuition fee receipt, the last academic qualification certificate, and bank details of the applicant or parent/guardian. Similar to the pre-matric scheme, the source notes that the scheme is implemented offline by DEPwD, while its application process section specifies online application through NSP.
